changelog: 2026-08-09: Added benchmark_evidence references, updated n8n status (RUNNING confirmed), added Ruflo DEFERRED entry, added decision_criteria based on W1 evidence, added engine_selection_matrix

strategies.benchmark_evidence: Used in W1 — exec tool called 14 times for file/shell operations. Zero failures. Latency: <1s per call.
strategies.decision_criteria: Choose this when: output is deterministic, no reasoning required, task is well-specified as a command.

strategies.validation_requirements: output review + deterministic test where possible
strategies.benchmark_evidence: W1 used this strategy — single OpenClaw/Alusi subagent with exec tools completed a full repository audit at quality=5/5 in 188s. Cost < $0.05.
strategies.decision_criteria: Choose this when: task fits in one context window, reasoning needed but no parallelism benefit, low-medium stakes. Default strategy for most agent tasks.

strategies.benchmark_evidence: W1 is exactly this pattern — OpenClaw/Alusi subagent used exec, read, process tools to gather evidence before synthesizing. 188s, quality 5/5. Confirms this is highest-value strategy for analysis tasks.
strategies.decision_criteria: Choose this when: task requires accessing external state (files, APIs, DBs) AND reasoning about that state. Primary strategy for audit, debugging, implementation tasks.

strategies.quality_profile: good per lane — requires merge validation
strategies.cost_profile: 2-5x token multiplier — justified only by wall-clock savings
strategies.selection_gate: CAN work products be generated independently WITHOUT shared state? If NO — do not use.
strategies.benchmark_evidence: Not yet benchmarked. W8 (parallel sub-agents) designed but not yet executed. Ruflo was listed as preferred engine for this strategy but is DEFERRED/BROKEN.
strategies.ruflo_status: DEFERRED — CLI broken, not installable. Fall back to OpenClaw Sessions/subagents for parallelism.
strategies.decision_criteria: Choose when: N independent tasks exist, wall-clock time matters, and you accept 2-5x token cost. Do NOT use for tasks with shared mutable state.

strategies.cost_profile: high — use when task complexity justifies it
strategies.benchmark_evidence: Antfarm (W1 target) confirmed capable — 3 workflows installed (bug-fix/feature-dev/security-audit), each with 6-7 specialized agents. Database shows prior production runs (60KB DB with WAL). n8n also confirmed RUNNING as of 2026-08-09 — available for workflow integration.
strategies.decision_criteria: Choose when: task has multiple phases, each requiring different expertise, and phases depend on prior phase outputs. Antfarm is preferred for dev workflows; n8n for API/webhook orchestration.

best_task_patterns: difficult bugs with multiple viable solutions
strategies.validation_requirements: adversarial review + judge decision + deterministic test
strategies.selection_gate: Use ONLY for high-risk/high-value. Never for routine tasks.
strategies.benchmark_evidence: Not yet benchmarked. Both Claude Code (v2.1.140) and Codex (v0.129.0) confirmed installed and available. Hermes not yet available (deps unmet).
strategies.decision_criteria: Reserve for: security architecture decisions, capital allocation controls, irreversible migrations. Cost floor is 2x single-agent. Quality ceiling is highest available.

strategies.benchmark_evidence: n8n confirmed RUNNING 2026-08-09 (healthz OK, port 5678). Prior registry had it as NOT_RUNNING — CORRECTED. Antfarm DB shows 60KB of prior workflow runs. Both engines ready for event-driven tasks NOW.
strategies.decision_criteria: Choose when: task repeats on a schedule or trigger, logic is stable enough to codify in a workflow, human oversight at decision points rather than execution steps.

strategies.benchmark_evidence: Approval system confirmed operational — sovereign_proxy + telegram-approvals (PM2 id 14) + alusi-controlled-worker (PM2 id 5) all RUNNING. No formal benchmark needed — production evidence from daily ops.
strategies.decision_criteria: ALWAYS use when: money moves, secrets change, production data at risk, legal/compliance implications. Gate is Telegram approval from Nathan. Never bypass.

engine_selection_matrix.description: Quick-reference for choosing the right engine given task type. Based on W1 benchmark evidence + verification data from 2026-08-09.

matrix.evidence: W1: 188s, quality 5/5, full structural audit of antfarm repo
W1 confirms Antfarm is installed, operational, with 60KB of prior runs
Ruflo not available — fall back to OpenClaw parallelism

openai_tier3.use_when: free path exhausted OR task requires tool_compatibility + cost <$0.001

openai_tier4.use_when: premium reasoning OR complex coding OR long_context with quality gate

ruflo_status.reason: CLI not found on system. Binary not in PATH, not in ~/.openclaw recursively. No installable package identified.
ruflo_status.action: Investigate Ruflo installation method in next PMO review cycle
ruflo_status.impact: PARALLEL_SPECIALISTS strategy falls back to OpenClaw Sessions/subagents — capable but not Ruflo-optimized

needs_test_seeding: W2 (Antfarm bug-fix — test repo with seeded bug)

selection_guidance: PMO must evaluate: complexity, parallelizability, quality threshold, latency, cost, risk, coordination overhead. Never select more agents merely because more are available.
key_principle: Use cheapest strategy that reliably satisfies quality and time thresholds.

evidence_based_defaults.default_for_analysis: SINGLE_AGENT_PLUS_TOOLS via OpenClaw/Alusi — proven at quality 5/5 in W1
evidence_based_defaults.default_for_pipelines: Antfarm — confirmed installed with prior runs, or n8n (now confirmed RUNNING)
